findings.evidence: None of SOURCES 1-8 publishes a release/version identifier for the ProgramBench board: programbench.com and /extended/ carry only an update stamp ("Updated Sep. 28, 2026") and task count ("200 tasks"); the registry README, main README, submission.py and ignored_tests.json contain no version. Under criterion c2, "published" requires the maintainer to publish a release identifier that the row's `version` copies; since none is published the row should be "snapshot" with version "snapshot-<date>". The row instead declares version "1" and version_status "published", which asserts a maintainer release identifier that the captured protocol does not provide.
findings.repair: Change version_status to "snapshot" and version to "snapshot-<date>" reflecting the captured methodology date; or, if a maintainer-published release identifier genuinely exists, document it and keep "published". status "active" and superseded_by null remain correct per criteria.

uncertainties: I could not recompute row/owner hashes or execute transport/qualification checks (read-only critic); I rely on the supplied sha256 bindings (row f0cbecfb…, owner ab9ee134…).
Unit "percent" and range [0,100] agree with the served mean_score values (lowest 16, highest 74.7 per SOURCE 10), and the protocol need not state the scale, so no finding there.

Several version_guard phrases (exact ten-field schema, unique model per row, providers) are consistent with SOURCE 2 but not all are independently countable from the excerpt; not treated as failures for c1/c2.

Maintainer field includes "Princeton University & Meta"; Meta appears via the page copyright, while Princeton is not explicit in the provided excerpts (paper bib lists authors only); treated as descriptive rather than a criterion field.
